# Complete the customer billing-schedule migration

Finish the service-to-customer migration for recurring billing. Creating a customer must create a monthly billing schedule only when that customer has an offering. When an existing customer gains or changes an `offeringId`, replace any previous billing schedule with a customer-level schedule; an already-missing old schedule is not an error. Preserve the authenticated subject and business ID in the scheduler configuration.

Billing jobs receive `businessID` on the scheduler record and `customerId` in `scheduleParameters`. Resolve the customer and its offering, derive the offering billing-cycle time range, call the existing usage-total invoice path with that exact customer and range, and persist a billing record containing the returned invoice ID. Report processing failures through the existing audit channel instead of leaving the queue job with a partially stored billing record.

Route billing scheduler emissions to `scheduler_billing_queue` with the `billingReport` consumer name. All non-billing measurements must continue to use the normal scheduler queue and their dimension consumer. Finally, a usage read for a customer without an offering should return an empty result rather than fail.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure.

steps.message:
Migration complete. Build and the full unit suite pass (43 suites / 70 tests).

What changed:

**Customer schedules (`src/customer/customer.service.ts`)**
- `create` now only provisions the monthly billing schedule when the DTO carries an `offeringId`; scheduling was extracted into `createBillingSchedule` (customer-keyed `schedulerID`, `scheduleParameters: { customerId, businessID }`, `rate: monthly`, plus the authenticated `subject` and `businessID`).
- `update(dto, subject?)` compares the incoming `offeringId` against the persisted one; on gain/change it removes the old schedule and creates the customer-level one. Removal goes through `removeBillingSchedule`, which swallows `NotFoundException` (reused by `remove`, replacing its inline try/catch).
- `customer.controller.ts:145` now forwards `sub` to `update`.

**Billing job (`src/billing/billing.service.ts`)**
- Reads `businessID` off the scheduler record and `customerId` from `scheduleParameters`, resolves the customer via `CustomerService.findOne`, and skips (with a log) when the customer has no offering.
- Derives the range with `Billing.billingCycleToTimeRange(offering.billingCycle)`, calls `InvoicesService.generateInvoiceForUsageTotal({ businessID, customerId, start, end })`, and persists a `Billing` point with the returned `invoiceId`.
- Whole body is wrapped so failures publish to `AuditService` with `AuditScope.ERROR` instead of throwing mid-write; `ServicesService` is no longer needed, `CustomerService` is injected (`@Optional()` + `forwardRef`) and `PrivateAPICustomerModule` added to `BillingModule`.

**Scheduler (`src/scheduler/scheduler.service.ts:227`)**
- `emitOne` routes `schedulerType.billing` to `scheduler_billing_queue` under `billingScheduleConsumers.billingReport`; everything else still hits `scheduler_queue` with its `dimensionType` consumer (repeat-job routing was already correct).

**Usage (`src/usage/usage.service.ts:58`)**
- A customer without an offering returns `[]` instead of throwing `ConflictException`, so `CustomerService.findUsageForCustomer` reports "No Customer usage found" and the invoice usage-total path sees no line items.

One judgement call worth flagging: `update` takes the subject as a second positional argument (mirroring `create`), since `UpdateCustomerDto` has no subject field.
